title: Central London Third Places — place properties, v0
description: Single source of truth for fields. Both scripts/validate.py and the site's filter UI derive from this file; nothing may hand-maintain a second list of fields elsewhere.
$comment: PROVISIONAL. This is schema v0, written before the survey (docs/PLAN.md step 1) has happened. It is expected to be wrong. In particular: payment_to_enter and payment_to_sit may well collapse into a single payment field, or split into three (enter / sit / stay beyond an hour) — walking fifty places is what decides that, not discussion. Optimise every change here for cheap replacement over cleverness. Judgement fields carry x-filter metadata so the reading surface can generate its filters from this file alone.

common.$comment: Every judgement field below is nullable on purpose. Null means nobody has looked yet, and is a prompt to go and sit there. A guessed value is a lie, and after the fact there is no way to tell one from the other.

id.description: OSM element or Overture GERS identifier. Every place is keyed to one so deduplication is a primary-key lookup rather than fuzzy name matching.

name.description: The name the place is known by. Not a description.

payment_to_enter.description: Whether money changes hands to get through the door.

values.none: nothing to pay at the door
values.required: a ticket or fee is required

payment_to_sit.description: Whether money changes hands to occupy a seat once inside. Distinct from entry: plenty of free-to-enter places still expect a purchase before you sit down.

values.optional: a cafe exists, but sitting without buying is accepted

time_pressure.description: Whether staying a long time becomes uncomfortable.

values.none: stay as long as you like
values.implied: no rule, but you feel it after a while
values.enforced: a stated time limit, or someone asks

conversation.description: Whether talking is permitted. Not whether it happens.

values.possible: you can talk without being out of place

activity.description: Whether doing something other than the place's nominal purpose — reading, working, drawing, waiting — is permitted.

values.discouraged: you are expected to be here for the stated purpose
values.possible: nobody minds what you are doing
values.expected: the place is set up for it

seating.description: The dominant seating type. Movable matters more than comfortable: it is what lets people form a group.

setting.description: Shelter, which decides whether a place works in bad weather.

support_options.description: Ways to give the place money if you want to. DISPLAY ONLY — never scored, never sorted on, never used to order anything. A place with none is not worse than a place with four.

why.description: One sentence on why this place is here. The only free text in the schema, capped so it stays a sentence rather than a review. Null only on desk-seeded candidates, which nobody has been to yet.

verified.description: True means Cormac has physically sat there. False means desk-seeded from OSM and unvisited. The two must never be silently mixed on the reading surface.

verified_date.description: ISO date the attributes were last checked in person. Decay logic is off, but the date is recorded from day one because retrofitting it later is miserable.

osm_tags.description: Raw OSM tags kept verbatim from seeding, for provenance and for re-deriving fields when the schema changes. Not displayed, and not a place to smuggle free text into.

then.$comment: A verified place without a date is not verified, it is a claim.

candidate.$comment: Desk-seeded and unvisited. Almost every judgement field is null, and that is correct. Used for data/candidates.geojson.

place.$comment: The published corpus. Everything a candidate must satisfy, plus a human sentence. Used for data/places.geojson.
